title: The kit's scripts put the repository root on sys.path only to import tools (A31)

context.task: Close A31 in the form that stays in the v0.1: a module at the root of a repository with the kit, named like a standard-library module (a project's own logging.py, inspect.py or dataclasses.py), must not be imported by the kit's scripts. Today it is, because every script puts the root first on sys.path and keeps it there; the gates then fail closed or the validator does not start, although nobody attacks.

select.heading: A31 — La raíz del repositorio va delante de la biblioteca estándar en las puertas
2. A31: la raíz del repositorio va delante de la biblioteca estándar
5.2 Hooks y `commit_integrity.py`: `-I -S`, y la raíz solo para importar `tools`

problem: Nine scripts of the kit do `if str(REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))` and then import: the hooks require_boundary_validation.py, require_contract_context.py and announce_governance.py, tools/git/commit_integrity.py (run by the pre-commit), tools/boundary_validator/validator.py (the MCP server), tools/install.py, and the audit scripts build_review_package.py, delegation_contract.py and verify_red_green.py. The root stays first on sys.path, so every later import of a standard-library module that is not loaded yet (dataclasses through project_config, sqlite3 through hook_gate, ast through primitives, subprocess through run_process, logging in the validator) loads a file of the same name at the root instead (CASES.md, A31, reproduced at hook level in a clone). A cooperative project that has its own logging.py or inspect.py at its root breaks the kit without anybody attacking: the hooks fail closed and deny, the validator does not start, the pre-commit or the audit scripts fail. Interpreter options do not change it: the insert is done by the scripts' own code. Putting the root last is not a fix either: on this machine the interpreter's site-packages holds a foreign top-level package named tools, which would shadow the kit in the validator (ARRANQUE_PUERTAS.md 5.2).
decisions: D1 The pattern, in each of the nine scripts of the problem: insert the root at position 0 only if it is not already in sys.path, `import tools`, then remove the root again if this code inserted it. The kit's submodules then load through tools.__path__, and no later import, of the standard library or of a third party, searches the root. When the root was already on sys.path (pytest's conftest), nothing is removed. Every import of a submodule of tools stays as it is today, after `import tools`.

D2 In require_boundary_validation.py, require_contract_context.py, announce_governance.py and commit_integrity.py the pattern sits inside the existing fail-closed `try`, so that a failure of `import tools` or of the removal still ends in the existing handler and its exit status (2 for the hooks), never in an unhandled exception that exits 1, which the harness reads as a broken hook and not as a denial (AGENTS 6.5: each edit leaves the hook working).

D3 In validator.py the root is removed before `import logging` and `from pydantic import ...`, so that neither is ever searched at the root; the kit's own submodules are imported after `import tools`. Nothing else in its start-up changes: no sys.path guard, no interpreter options and no refusal to start (those belong to A19, which goes to the v0.2).

D4 One helper or nine copies is the implementer's choice, with one condition: the scripts cannot import a helper from tools before tools itself is imported, so a shared helper is not possible and the pattern is written in each script; a test checks that the nine copies are the same lines, as the copies of `canonical` are checked today.

D5 Out of scope, unchanged: the hook commands in .claude/settings.json, .mcp.json and opencode.jsonc, tools/git/pre-commit, the shim, interpreter options (-I, -S), the PATH (A32), sitecustomize and .pth files (A19), hook decisions and messages, and the validator's responses.

D6 The new tests work on a copy of the kit in tmp_path (installed with tools/install.py as tests/unit/test_installer.py does, or copied from the working tree), never on the real repository root, where the live hooks of the session would load anything planted. At the copy's root they plant dataclasses.py, sqlite3.py, logging.py, ast.py, inspect.py and subprocess.py; each one appends its name to a witness file outside the copy and then loads the real module, so a script that imports it still works. Each script is run as a program, with the interpreter the tests run under, on an input that reaches its imports: a payload for each hook, nothing staged for commit_integrity.py, a ping over stdio for the validator, --dry-run on a throwaway target for install.py, and --help or another read-only form for the audit scripts. A script for which no planted module is imported at base is reported as such, not forced.
D7 For each script the test also runs the same input on a copy without the planted modules and asserts the same exit status and output, so that the fix changes what is imported, not what is decided.

D8 The session's validator requires a Rationale in every proposal (AGENTS.md 2.2). The schema of validate_proposal shown in this session may be an older copy without it: include it anyway, or the proposal comes back INVALID_JSON. The running server keeps the code it started with; a change to validator.py reaches it at the next session.
D9 No new dependency and no new network, process or code-loading primitive in a governed Python file; a test that starts a process uses tools/audit/run_process.py.

D11 Amendment (2026-10-15, after the first run stopped on it): two existing tests pin the non-standard imports of a script, and D1's bare `import tools` adds one. In tests/security/test_contract_context_hook.py, test_hook_imports_only_the_standard_library_and_the_project_configuration expects {"tools", "tools.project_config"}; in tests/security/test_commit_integrity.py, ALLOWED_KIT_IMPORTS gains "tools". Nothing else changes in those two files. It is a change of the specification made by D1, not a test changed to hide a failure (AGENTS 8.2).

D12 In the report, the cases of the T1 test that do not import a planted module at base (build_review_package.py and delegation_contract.py, which import their standard-library modules before the old insert) go under an X id with the expectation guard, not under T1, so that T1 holds only cases that are red at base.

D10 Gates: red-first, each red test seen failing for its stated reason before the change that makes it pass; full-suite, `pytest tests/` exits 0 at the commit; hooks-every-environment, tests/security/test_hooks_without_shim.py passes; verify-red-green, tools/audit/verify_red_green.py exits 0 on the report.

behaviours.statement: With dataclasses.py, sqlite3.py, logging.py, ast.py, inspect.py and subprocess.py planted at the root of a kit copy, none of the nine scripts imports any of them: the witness file stays empty for every script and input of D6.

Each script gives the same exit status and output with and without the planted modules (D7): the boundary hook still denies an Edit on a governed path without a receipt, the validator still answers ping, install.py still prints its plan.
After each script's start-up, the root is not on sys.path unless it was there before; when it was there before (as under pytest), it is still there.
In each hook and in commit_integrity.py, a failure while importing tools still ends in the existing fail-closed handler: the hooks exit 2 with their message, never 1.

The validator imports logging and pydantic with the root off sys.path, and the kit's tools with it on; with a foreign top-level package named tools importable from site-packages, it still loads the kit's tools.
The nine copies of the pattern are the same lines.

tests.must_catch: a hook, commit_integrity.py, the validator, install.py or an audit script that imports a module planted at the root of a kit copy
tests.reason: today every script keeps the root first on sys.path, so the planted modules are imported (CASES.md, A31)

tests.must_catch: a script that leaves the root on sys.path after its start-up when it was not there before, or removes it when it was
tests.reason: today the root is inserted and never removed

tests.must_catch: a validator that loads a foreign top-level tools package instead of the kit's, or that searches the root for logging or pydantic
tests.reason: today the validator searches the root first for every import after the insert

tests.must_catch: copies of the pattern that differ between the nine scripts
tests.reason: today there is no pattern to compare, only the insert

tests.must_catch: a script whose exit status or output changes with the fix, or a hook that fails open when tools cannot be imported
tests.reason: today the scripts decide the same with and without the planted modules on a clean copy, and the hooks exit 2 when the import fails; both must keep holding

commit_message: fix(puertas): la raíz entra en sys.path solo para importar tools y sale enseguida (A31)
